A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hydra Ensembles research, with matching authors, method, principal experiments, and appendices. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison. Localized reporting inconsistencies in v2 do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image classification, text classification, zero-shot classification, OOD detection, runtime, and pruning-ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds diversity measurements, ensemble-size and fusion experiments, repeated-seed summaries, and corruption-robustness results.

M1.justification: The Taylor/circuit head-pruning strategies, independent member fine-tuning, grouped attention fusion, and weight-averaged MLP merging remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix D. Five-member and non-fused models are additional experimental configurations, not revisions to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The datasets, domains, and classification/OOD tasks are retained. ImageNet-C and CIFAR-100-C already appear in v1 Appendix B.1; v2's severity-wise ImageNet-C tables expand analysis within existing corruption coverage rather than introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds Taylor and CircAvg to the inference-cost comparison, previously limited to Single, Deep Ensembles, and Hydra. v2 Table 9 also includes Deep Ensembles as a reference for direct diversity measurements. The principal benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantial evaluation designs: ID/OOD mutual information and disagreement measurements, three-versus-five-member comparisons, fused-versus-non-fused controls, and accuracy/Brier evaluation at five corruption severities (Tables 9–14). Existing training recipes and benchmark splits remain unchanged; these are additional protocols rather than evidence that the original experiments were rerun differently.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's head-selection, pruning-strength, and randomness-source analyses, v2 directly measures ensemble diversity, tests ensemble-size tradeoffs, and evaluates whether MLP fusion affects predictive performance (Appendices B.5–B.7). Appendix E.1 adds comparative corruption-robustness results, substantially extending the evidence about the method's behavior.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates and seed-source ablations without across-run uncertainty summaries. v2 Table 12 newly reports means and standard deviations across eight seeds for Hydra Ensembles (Circ) on ImageNet-1K and CIFAR-100. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, but does not establish how many runs were performed for v1.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 9–14 add diversity, ensemble-size, fusion, repeated-seed, and corruption results while retaining the main Hydra scores. BayesVLM's CIFAR-100 accuracy changes from 71.14 to 75.61 (v1 Table 18 versus v2 Table 24), reversing its ranking against Hydra's unchanged 74.87; its average accuracy changes from 73.15 to 73.64. v2 Table 26 also adds BayesVLM OOD values alongside the old values without clearly identifying replacements.

T1.justification: The clean/noisy-data assumptions, Proposition 1, Taylor-expansion proof, fusion equations, and parameter-count derivations are retained. The new empirical diversity metrics are named without introducing revised mathematical definitions or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about uncertainty-aware head pruning, efficient transformer ensembling, and competitive uncertainty estimation with near-single-model inference cost. The additional experiments support existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds a mechanism explanation for why post-training MLP fusion preserves attention-driven diversity, interprets the cost-benefit of additional members, and asserts seed insensitivity and transfer to corruption robustness (Appendices B.6–B.7 and E.1). These substantially extend the interpretation, although the blanket robustness and insensitivity language is stronger than the reported evidence warrants.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix C.3 newly specify the zero-shot prompt template, "A photo of a {label}." This is additional reproducibility information, not a documented change of prompt. Dataset sources were already disclosed in v1 Appendix C.3; detailed implementation recipes and the promised code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier pruning and uncertainty methods remain unchanged. The added Hendrycks and Dietterich 2019b reference is the conference version of the corruption-benchmark work already cited, rather than a newly introduced research work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved. Local changes include new appendix subsections B.6–B.7, expanded explanatory paragraphs, a rewritten opening to E.1, an acknowledgments section, and conference-publication headers. There is no extensive rewriting of the existing exposition.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially with dedicated diversity, member-count, fusion, seed-summary, and corruption-severity tables. Table 7 gains comparator rows, and existing tables are redistributed and renumbered; Figures 1–7 remain unchanged. v2 Table 26 additionally introduces confusing unlabeled pairs of values within BayesVLM cells.

improvement.justification: The direct diversity measurements, fusion controls, eight-seed summaries, and corruption tests strengthen validation of the retained method and address questions left untested in v1. Reporting problems limit the gain: Table 26 leaves paired BayesVLM values unexplained, Tables 3 and 24 disagree on its average aECE (5.86 versus 5.68), and Appendix E.1 overstates robustness despite Table 14 showing Hydra (Circ) has worse average Brier than Single (0.59 versus 0.58).
